known_facts: The Mindbloom Petal can restore a mind, but it can also shatter it if the harvester's intent is not pure.
The legend is not just about the petal, but about the 'balance' it represents.

CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE: The petal is etheric and will be destroyed by any contact with mundane metal. It must be harvested with a tool of pure, natural materials, such as polished obsidian or ancient bone.
The Whispering Caves where the petal grows are dangerous and filled with deceptive echoes.
I know that Baelor the Blacksmith is the only one in the village who has the 'pure heart' and 'steady hands' required to craft an obsidian tool, though I doubt he remembers the ancient technique.
Moonpetal Salve, brewed from silverleaf and morning dew, closes a wound overnight, but only if it is applied before the wound festers.
Silverleaf grows only on the north bank of Serpent's Creek, and only in the three weeks after the spring thaw.
Fever-root must be boiled twice; boiled only once, it worsens the very fever it is meant to cure.
Bitterthorn tea dulls pain but clouds judgement, so I never give it to anyone who is about to travel.
The Blue Moon rises once every nineteen years, and every child born under it carries some imbalance.
The deepest chamber of the Whispering Caves is called the Hollow, and no lantern will stay lit inside it.
My grandmother taught me that the woods answer honestly, but only to those who ask without wanting anything.
